signature: completion resolves 2xx but the final assistant message has empty content, no tool_call blocks, stop_reason=stop (PoC: terminal empty assistant event 15-17 ms after tool results, rc=0 clean exit; NOT a timeout, NOT an API error)
required_behavior: retry the turn with a FRESH seed (never an identical body+seed pair) inside the same session; count the phase attempt; at cap bank the session and end the phase attempt, escalating per the phase retry accounting (never silent)
max_retries_or_bound: engine.phase_attempt_cap (default 3; PoC discovered default RETRY_CAP=3)

signature: empty completion (FM-01 signature) AND the session transcript is in the provider's size-ceiling band — measured deaths at 496,294 B and 496,578 B, 284 B apart, after similar 16-18 min lifespans (deterministic transcript-size ceiling, not random failure)
required_behavior: at the early-warning threshold refuse NEW corpus ingestion and bank the session at the next turn boundary; at the hard ceiling end the session at the boundary and cold-boot a compacted successor session; never truncate a live transcript mid-flight (L8 audit integrity); mechanism policy per DR-06
max_retries_or_bound: transcript_ceiling_warn_bytes (default 450,000) / transcript_ceiling_hard_bytes (default 496,000; per-provider override)

signature: seed-0 replay loop: >=2 consecutive byte-identical request bodies / byte-identical assistant replies at identical sampling params (engine pins DEFAULT_SEED=0; identical (body, sampling params) replays byte-identically at ANY temperature; a failed call that does not mutate state produces an identical retry body)
required_behavior: prevented by default: the loop varies the seed per request, fill-if-absent (explicit seed wins for replay tooling); every RETRY gets a fresh seed; the dedup guard (canonical-text uniqueness, I01 L14 schema half) mutates the body at turn 1; alert on repetition
max_retries_or_bound: prevented-by-default (no retry bound; repetition is a tripwire signal, ENTRY 7)

signature: tool wedge: transcript ends at an unanswered tool_call while the engine is fully idle (no in-flight request) and the session is frozen past the per-call deadline — the tool-call layer never returns (PoC: grep-tool class B, five ACTIVITY_TIMEOUT kills in 7h)
required_behavior: every tool call runs under a deadline watchdog that kills the tool's process GROUP with TERM->grace->liveness-probe->KILL escalation and returns a LOUD teaching refusal (what ran: pattern/path/glob, elapsed, how to narrow); the session survives and routes around it; never an unbounded wait (pgroup hygiene wherever subprocesses exist)
max_retries_or_bound: tool_timeout_s (default 120; worst-case wall timeout + ~17 s)

signature: timeout: Fast::Completions::TimeoutError raised — the watchdog fires on TTFB (no response headers within the deadline) or on read inactivity between body chunks (re-armed after every chunk); distinct from a user cancel
required_behavior: bounded retry with jittered exponential backoff ABOVE the gem's own immediate creation retry (which re-arms the deadline per attempt); each retry carries a fresh seed; at the bound end the phase attempt and escalate; never wedge on a hung request
max_retries_or_bound: engine.transport_retry_cap (default 3; gem Client timeout default 30 s, ttfb/inactivity overrides per call)

signature: connection error at creation: Fast::Completions::ConnectionError raised with no 2xx received (ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET/EPIPE/EHOSTUNREACH/ENETUNREACH/ETIMEDOUT/EOFError/IOError/SocketError)
required_behavior: bounded retry with jittered backoff; after the cap probe provider/gateway health and fail the phase attempt loudly (never wedge, never silent retry forever); a usage_events row is recorded for the failed call (zero tokens — the call is still an event)
max_retries_or_bound: engine.transport_retry_cap (default 3)

signature: provider 429: Fast::Completions::RateLimitError (HTTP 429; the gem retries 408/409/429/5xx at creation up to max_retries, and honors x-should-retry:false as FINAL regardless of status)
required_behavior: honor Retry-After / x-should-retry; jittered exponential backoff with a class-specific (longer) cap; at the bound stop the phase attempt and escalate-to-pause (a rate-limited provider is an operator-visible condition, not a loop problem); spend row recorded per failed call
max_retries_or_bound: engine.rate_limit_retry_cap (default 5)

signature: provider 5xx: Fast::Completions::ServerError (HTTP 500-599)
required_behavior: bounded jittered retry; after the cap fail the phase attempt and escalate (route to the never-reportless finisher discipline, ENTRY 6 — a budget/stop exit must never be silently reportless); spend row recorded per failed call
max_retries_or_bound: engine.server_error_retry_cap (default 3)

signature: context length exceeded: Fast::Completions::ContextLengthExceededError — a 400 whose body matches a provider context-overflow pattern (the gem ports the pattern set as data)
required_behavior: NEVER retry the same body; shrink the context (compact the transcript, drop the largest blocks, re-assemble via the ContextBudgeter) and re-issue once; if unshrinkable, bank the session at the boundary and cold-boot a compacted successor (same ceiling machinery as FM-02)
max_retries_or_bound: shrink retry bound: 1, then bank-and-compact (model context_window is the authority)

signature: dialect mismatch: Fast::Completions::BadRequestError (400) with no context-overflow pattern — the provider rejects a dialect-carried request field (max_tokens field name, developer role, store, reasoning_effort, thinking format); unknown dialect keys/values raise ArgumentError at DECLARATION time, not on the wire
required_behavior: fail loud and refuse any silent translation: name the dialect key in question in the error surfaced to the operator; the quest is paused (not killed) for provider reconfiguration via the seam; a mis-declared dialect is a config defect, never a runtime retry
max_retries_or_bound: dialect declaration is boot-time fail-loud (no runtime bound)

signature: malformed tool call: a tool_call block's arguments finalize to the ToolArgumentsFailure marker (non-empty arguments scratch that fails the whole-buffer parse even after the control-character repair walk — duplicated or truncated arguments stream); never a silent empty-arguments fallback
required_behavior: surface the marker as that call's is_error tool result carrying the marker message verbatim (the model re-calls the tool); never execute a malformed call; count per session as a stream-honesty signal for ENTRY 7 tripwires
max_retries_or_bound: in-band (the model self-corrects); per-session count is a tripwire input
evidence: repos/fast-llm/gems/completions/lib/fast/completions/errors.rb §tool call arguments are unparseable JSON at stream finalize

signature: unknown tool: the assistant names a tool absent from the session's registered surface (including subagent profile restrictions)
required_behavior: the harness finalizes the in-band error result per the gem contract ("no such tool: <name>") and ADDS the session's legal-tools list (profile-restricted surface for subagents) so the refusal teaches; the model re-calls; 3 consecutive unknown-tool calls escalate to a wedge-guard alert (a stuck model, not a bad call)
max_retries_or_bound: in-band; unknown_tool_alert_at (default 3 consecutive)

signature: stream truncation: Fast::Completions::StreamError raised after a client-level :error event — the stream ends without the finish_reason the dialect expects (including the case where a dropped chunk carried it), or the provider sends an error finish_reason
required_behavior: persist the salvaged partial and its usage to the transcript/ledger as audit (never auto-append a partial to the live history); retry the turn with a fresh seed; at the cap bank the session and end the phase attempt
max_retries_or_bound: engine.stream_retry_cap (default 2)

signature: dropped wire chunks: Client#dropped_chunks > 0 after a turn — a chunk unparseable after SSE rejoin + the repair walk is dropped and counted, never raised; the stream continues to its natural terminal (tolerant inbound-stream class)
required_behavior: the gem already tolerates (drop-and-continue — the loop must NOT re-add strictness); record the count per session; at threshold alert as a serving-stack health signal feeding ENTRY 7 tripwires; note the residual risk: a dropped finish-carrying chunk lands in FM-13, a lost arguments fragment in FM-11
max_retries_or_bound: dropped_chunk_alert_threshold (default 3 per session)

signature: mid-stream connection failure after 2xx: a NETWORK-family exception while the body streams — the client-level :error event carries the SALVAGED partial (every streamed block + usage so far, reasoning_details serialized exactly as a completed finalize would) before ConnectionError raises; a retry is structurally impossible (attempt committed to streaming)
required_behavior: persist the salvaged partial AND its usage to the transcript/ledger and record the usage_events row from the salvaged usage (tokens were spent); retry the turn with a fresh seed; at the bound end the phase attempt
max_retries_or_bound: engine.transport_retry_cap (default 3)

signature: one-writer violation: a session launch (orchestrator phase attempt or operator interactive attach) finds the quest already held by a live writer — a session row with ended_at IS NULL whose owning worker is alive (I01 DR-12 pinned the enforcement home: the orchestrator's launch path + reaper, NOT a schema constraint — a partial unique on unfinished sessions would block L7 cold-boot)
required_behavior: refuse the second writer loudly, naming the holder session and its driver; never queue a write behind a live writer; the refused launch returns the holder's identity so the operator can pause-and-resume; the ToolHarness write-guard rechecks the gate before every mutation batch as defense-in-depth
max_retries_or_bound: terminal (no retry); enforcement points: session-start gate + per-batch write-guard recheck

signature: budget ceiling: a turn-boundary rollup over usage_events (token spend) or the web-call rollup over tool_calls reaches the quest's configured cap (L9: web calls AND token spend, live-re-readable at phase boundaries)
required_behavior: stop starting new turns at the boundary; route to the never-reportless finisher discipline (synthesis, or an explicit loud stop — ENTRY 6); pause the quest for the operator; a budget stop must never be silently reportless (PoC: every organic budget/cap exit was reportless, twice requiring operator intervention)
max_retries_or_bound: quests token_budget / web_call_budget (config values; PoC web caps 1400/300)

signature: SLOWSTALL: the live session transcript grows < 100 bytes over >= 20 minutes while the session state is running (expected pace under slow local models; the operator's authoritative stall signal, deliberately replacing counter-based tripwires)
required_behavior: ALERT only — the alert text carries the driver-NOT-to-be-killed-on-this-alone rule; never auto-kill on growth alone; if the unattended window elapses, pause the quest for the operator rather than kill; feed the signal to ENTRY 7
max_retries_or_bound: slow_stall_bytes=100 / slow_stall_window_s=1200 (alert); unattended_pause_s (default 3600)

signature: operator pause request while a turn is in flight (quest lifecycle active->paused; the in-flight turn may be completable at its boundary or must be cancelled)
required_behavior: deliver pause at the turn boundary when the turn can complete (bank it); else cancel the in-flight turn — CancelledError surfaces with NO phantom terminal event and the half-streamed turn is never appended to history; committed mutations survive (L7); config is re-read at resume; steering lands only through pause, never while running (D5)
max_retries_or_bound: pause_grace: prefer turn boundary; hard cancel at phases.wall_timeout_s

signature: subagent spawn wedge: the spawn tool call never returns a result while the spawned child is provably healthy — the tool-call layer loses track of a spawn it successfully made (PoC wedge #3: dispatch-level tool-babysitter; "no tool result" does NOT imply "no process")
required_behavior: every spawn is a command that RETURNS IMMEDIATELY (detach); verification is ALWAYS a separate command keyed by run id against the run registry; never infer child death from a missing tool result; status polling by run id, deadline-bounded per run
max_retries_or_bound: subagent_status_poll_s (default 30) per run; subagent_timeout_s (default 1800) run deadline

signature: cold-boot orphans: a boot scan finds sessions with ended_at IS NULL whose owning worker is gone (crashed/killed session) — committed tool_calls/usage rows and graph mutations survive, the session row does not know it is dead
required_behavior: the reaper stamps ended_at on orphaned sessions (ledgered, no state column needed); the successor session reconstructs working state from durable reads ONLY (store-backed status/search/node reads — the PoC proved the exported file view stale while the store carried the truth); no in-memory-only state exists (L7) (classed retryable because the four-class enum has no recover class: the successor session is the bounded escalation — reap-and-reconstruct, not re-attempt)
max_retries_or_bound: reap on cold-boot scan + periodic sweep; liveness = worker registry (ENTRY 8), no heartbeat column needed

signature: context blowout by full-file corpus reads: context accounting shows source-text ingestion exceeding the session's slice budget (PoC: corpus file reads were 78% of the 79,677-token final context; S1 loaded ~122K chars before its first write; the single observed sliced re-read was 1.4K chars — the pattern that should have been the default)
required_behavior: enforce sliced reads (offset/limit) as the DEFAULT with a teaching refusal above the slice cap naming the offset/limit form; extract-as-you-read (never read-then-extract front-loading); retrieval-first via the hybrid seam before any full read; cold boots never re-read what a predecessor session already extracted
max_retries_or_bound: read_slice_cap_chars (default 8,000); transcript ceiling FM-02 as the backstop

signature: embedding call failure: an embed job's wire call to the registry-row endpoint returns HTTP 429/5xx, or raises ConnectionError/TimeoutError mid-batch (I03 deferred these retry classes to ENTRY 4)
required_behavior: bounded jittered retry per the loop's shared retry classes; resume is idempotent via the embed job idem key (J-IDEM: rerun = no-op resume; a failed attempt leaves a legal retry row); re-slice by registry batch_max_texts on readmission; usage row of kind=embedding recorded when tokens were spent (J-SPEND, tenancy-pinned)
max_retries_or_bound: embed_retry_cap (default 3) + registry batch_max_texts re-slice

signature: prefix-cache wall: at high context every turn pays a full re-prefill — cache_read=0 turn after turn; measured: a 262k window with an 8GiB prefix cache has an effective wall ~205k, above which every turn pays ~7 minutes of re-prefill (local serving of big-context synthesis is fragile)
required_behavior: keep the prompt prefix append-only within a session (stable prefix = cache hits); route mega-context phases (synthesis) per the routing config to cache-capable / large-window remote models; record cache_read/cache_write per call (DR-12 amendment) and alert on cache_read=0 at high context
max_retries_or_bound: provider cache_wall_tokens (config per provider; PoC-measured 205,000 for the local engine)

signature: missing spend row: a completion closes without a usage_events row, or ends with usage nil / all-zero on a dialect that declares supports_usage_in_streaming — spend would silently under-record (D10 cost honesty; failed calls cost tokens too)
required_behavior: SpendRecorder is a registered gem telemetry sink: exactly one terminal hook fires per completion (on_completion_end XOR on_completion_error), so the row is written even on error paths and consumer raises; nil/zero usage records a zero-token row (the call is still an event); a missing row at rollup time is an ENTRY 7 tripwire
max_retries_or_bound: gem contract: EXACTLY ONE terminal hook per completion (structural, not a retry bound)

signature: provider auth/permission/not-found: a FINAL 401/403/404 from the provider maps to the gem's AuthenticationError/PermissionError/NotFoundError status classes (never retried by the gem) — the realistic first-week cloud failure (stale api_key_ref, wrong model slug on a cloud route; the seam is cloud-ready day one per DR-01)
required_behavior: refuse loudly, the FM-10 fail-loud family: surface the mapped error class + status verbatim, do NOT retry (gem-final; the loop adds none), and pause the quest for credential/route reconfiguration via the provider seam — the operator reconfigures, then resumes
max_retries_or_bound: 0 retries (gem-final classes)
